---
title: "How to download a published model"
---

Published IBL Ephys Atlas models live on the Hugging Face Hub in **public** repositories.
This guide covers getting one, pinning a version, and verifying it works before you rely
on it.

## The available models

| Hugging Face repo | Family | Direction | Vintage |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost`](https://huggingface.co/int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost) | Region decoder | features → brain region, per channel | `2026_W42` |
| [`int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-transformer`](https://huggingface.co/int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-transformer) | Whole-probe region decoder | a probe's features → brain region per channel | `2026_W42` |
| [`int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-channel`](https://huggingface.co/int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-channel) | Spatial encoder | position → channel features | `2026_W44` |
| [`int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-unit`](https://huggingface.co/int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-unit) | Unit encoder | position → unit phenotype; units → putative cell types | `2026_W44` |

All four load through the same call. See [model families](../explanation/model-families.qmd)
for how they differ conceptually.

## One entry point

`load_pretrained` serves every family:

```python
from ephysatlas import load_pretrained

model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost", revision="2026_W42"
)
```

It resolves the id to a local directory, reads the publication manifest
(`ephysatlas_model.json`), and dispatches to the right wrapper class based on the
manifest's `model_class`. You do not choose the class — the model declares what it is.

As a result, a model card only has to name `load_pretrained`, and adding a new family
does not change any calling code.

## Pin a revision for reproducibility

```python
# Pinned: always loads the 2026_W42 release
model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost", revision="2026_W42"
)

# Not pinned: loads 'main', which changes when a new vintage is published
model = load_pretrained("int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost")
```

Without `revision=`, `load_pretrained` loads the `main` branch, which points to the
currently recommended model. When a new vintage is published, `main` moves to it, and the
same code then loads a different model and can return different predictions. Pin the
revision in any analysis you want to reproduce. `load_pretrained` logs a warning when no
revision is given:

```text
WARNING  no revision pinned for int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost: using 'main',
         which tracks the currently recommended model and will change when a new vintage
         is published. Pass revision='<vintage>' for a reproducible result.
```

Revision tags are **vintages** — `YYYY_Www` week labels matching the release the model
belongs to. A decoder and its features must come from the same vintage; see
[core concepts](../explanation/concepts.qmd). An encoder's `predict` takes only
positions, so it has no feature vintage to match.

`ephysatlas.models.DECODER_VINTAGES` holds the default vintage of each published region
decoder, the one the [alignment GUI](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ibl-alignment-gui/channel_prediction.html) loads unless told otherwise:

```python
from ephysatlas.models import DECODER_VINTAGES

DECODER_VINTAGES["int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost"]   # '2026_W42'
```

## Controlling where downloads land

By default files go to the standard Hugging Face cache. Override it with `cache_dir`:

```python
from pathlib import Path

model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost",
    revision="2026_W42",
    cache_dir=Path("/data/models"),
)
```

The download is cached, so a second call with the same id and revision is instant and
offline. Useful on a cluster: fetch once to a shared path, then point every job at it.

## Loading from a local directory

Pass a path instead of a repo id and nothing touches the network:

```python
model = load_pretrained("/data/models/ea-decoder-2026_W42")
```

`load_pretrained` checks whether the argument is an existing directory, and if so uses it
directly. This is the route for air-gapped machines, and for a model you have not
published yet.

Checksums are verified for local directories too — and **strictly**, with missing files
treated as an error, so an incomplete or hand-edited directory is caught rather than
half-loaded.

## Integrity is checked on load

Every published model ships `checksums.json`, a per-file digest of everything in the
release. `load_pretrained` re-hashes the files and compares:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import ephysatlas.model_registry

ephysatlas.model_registry.verify_checksums(Path("/data/models/ea-decoder-2026_W42"))
```

A truncated download, a file missing from the release, or a locally modified weight file
all fail this check. Files edited on the Hub after publication — the model card, the
licence, `.gitattributes` — are excluded from the manifest, so they never cause a spurious
failure.

## Verify your install reproduces the model

Checksums prove you have the right *bytes*. They say nothing about whether your Python
environment turns those bytes into the same numbers. That is what `selftest` is for:

```python
model.selftest()
# True
```

It re-predicts the example bundled with the model and compares against the shipped
expected output. It catches:

- a different XGBoost or PyTorch build whose numerics moved
- a NumPy or pandas upgrade that changed a dtype
- features whose units changed between vintages
- a reordered class vector

None of these raises an error; only the predictions change.

```python
try:
    model.selftest()
except FileNotFoundError:
    # A model that ships no example/ directory cannot self-test
    print("no golden files shipped; skipping")
```

Run it after every environment change.

## Inspect a model without predicting

The manifest describes the model, and a loaded model exposes it as `model.index`:

```python
index = model.index

index["model_id"]      # '2026_W42_Cosmos_flimsy-thistle-cat'
index["task"]          # 'region-classification'
index["vintage"]       # '2026_W42'
index["granularity"]   # 'channel'
index["model_class"]   # 'xgboost.sklearn.XGBClassifier'

index["inputs"]["table"]     # 'raw_ephys_features_denoised.pqt'
index["inputs"]["index"]     # ['pid', 'channel']
index["inputs"]["features"]  # the 48 required feature columns, in order
index["outputs"]             # what predict() returns

index["environment"]  # the exact versions the model was trained with
index["training"]     # seed, dataset sizes, training-set hash
```

`index["environment"]` is what to compare against when a self-test fails — it records the
Python, XGBoost, scikit-learn, NumPy and pandas versions used at training time.

Full field-by-field description: [model manifest reference](../reference/model-manifest.qmd).

## Troubleshooting

**`ValueError: ... has no ephysatlas_model.json; it is not a loadable model`** — the
directory is not a published model. Every release ships a manifest; one without it cannot
be loaded.

**`ValueError: ... declares model_class '...' which this version of ephysatlas cannot
load`** — the model is newer than your install. Upgrade ibleatools; the error lists the
`model_class` values your version knows.

**A checksum mismatch** — delete the cached download and re-fetch. If it recurs on a local
directory, a file there has been modified.

**`selftest` fails** — compare your versions against `model.index["environment"]`. Do not
work around it: a failing self-test means predictions from this install do not match the
published model.
